mbm-2501.clue: There's an address under the binding.
mbm-2501.quote: Before I sewed the edge of our moving-day quilt, my brother slipped our old address inside on a cloth label. Now whichever flat we live in, one corner already knows the way back.

mbm-2502.clue: The club's quietest spot has the best rhythm.
mbm-2502.quote: The floor shakes under the bench by the coat check. My friend sits there between dances and taps a spare pair of shoes to the bass. I take my breaks beside him.

mbm-2503.clue: I measure a train by its umbrellas.
mbm-2503.quote: From my platform bench I sketch the colored umbrellas reflected in the carriage windows. On a rainy morning one long silver train looks almost entirely made of flowers.

mbm-2504.clue: My tool roll has a place for a spoon.
mbm-2504.quote: I stitched a little leather roll for my punches. The final pocket holds the teaspoon Dad used to smooth edges before he could afford tools. It gets used on every piece I make.

mbm-2505.clue: My pajamas have a studio audience.
mbm-2505.quote: For game shows my family lines stuffed animals on the sofa arm. If we miss an easy question, the animals change sides. My mother's bear has an astonishing winning record.

mbm-2506.clue: My favorite trail marker is a red scarf.
mbm-2506.quote: I lost my red scarf on the ski trail and spotted it on a branch the next morning. A stranger had knotted it where nobody could ski past. We left it up till spring and called that bend hello.

mbm-2507.clue: I used to sing underneath the organ.
mbm-2507.quote: My voice disappeared behind the church organ at rehearsals, so I sat on the floor by the bench to learn my note from its pedals. The organist still leaves me room to find it.

mbm-2508.clue: My Frisbee can carry a drawing.
mbm-2508.quote: I sketched a tiny lighthouse on the underside. From across the park my friend sees the lighthouse blink through the disc whenever the sun catches it. He calls me in through the fog.

mbm-2509.clue: I lace one shoe in the dark.
mbm-2509.quote: I run early and leave everything ready by the door. My dog hears one lace pull and brings me the other shoe. I started putting a biscuit in it just for him.

mbm-2510.clue: The midnight show leaves one lamp on.
mbm-2510.quote: We stay till the old cinema's cleaner turns on an aisle lamp. He lets us turn the beam toward the curtain once, so my friends and I can bow to our own shadows.

mbm-2511.clue: I keep the chorus in my jacket pocket.
mbm-2511.quote: The DJ at my local club drew four little footmarks on a receipt to teach me a turn. The paper is soft as cloth now. When that song comes on I pat the pocket and step out.

mbm-2512.clue: The best pillow is still warm after sunset.
mbm-2512.quote: I spread a bath towel on the stone wall beside the beach. When my sunny patch slides away, the stones hold the heat. My little cousins sit there like a row of sleepy lizards.

mbm-2513.clue: My model can tell you when the mail comes.
mbm-2513.quote: I put my first finished mecha on the shelf above our mail slot. Every envelope through the door made the little antenna dance. Dad started delivering junk mail one piece at a time so he could watch the robot take attendance.

mbm-2514.clue: The pause screen saved our soup.
mbm-2514.quote: My flatmate paused our adventure game on a giant green dragon to stir dinner. When the lid came off, the soup was precisely that green. We've called it dragon broth ever since.

mbm-2515.quote: I put a folded note inside my partner's shoe before our first competition. She put a drawing of a dancing potato in mine. It is almost impossible to dance nervously with that in mind.

mbm-2516.clue: I save sand in a clock that doesn't work.
mbm-2516.quote: At our last beach volleyball game before my friend moved, we took one spoonful of sand and sealed it inside her cracked egg timer. There is always more time in that game.

mbm-2517.clue: My notebook has a hole where the sun goes.
mbm-2517.quote: I drew the outline of a plane in my spotting notebook and cut it out. Hold the page against the sky at the airfield and I have one little plane that always flies on time.

mbm-2518.clue: I slid the wrong bead in on purpose.
mbm-2518.quote: My sister likes her bracelets matched. I work one glass bead the color of her blue bicycle into each. When she layers them on her wrist the bicycles all line up.

mbm-2519.clue: My quiet song only needs one shoe.
mbm-2519.quote: My choir director asked me to go home and listen for the quietest sound in the house. I was tying a shoe when I heard the lace slip through the eyelet. I sang a lullaby to that tiny rhythm. My nephew still asks for the shoelace song.

mbm-2520.clue: I made my first radio contact under a tablecloth.
mbm-2520.quote: Our radio club set up at a summer fair and the glare hid the dials. I ducked under a checked tablecloth with the receiver like an old photographer. When I came back out I'd made my first contact and missed a whole puppet show.

mbm-2521.clue: My middle finger is the missing window.
mbm-2521.quote: I painted a little row of midnight houses across my nails. When I curl my fingers the lit window on my thumb slides into the house on my middle finger. Somebody just got home.

mbm-2522.clue: My first costume change was a tablecloth.
mbm-2522.quote: Our play needed a king in gold. I borrowed a patterned cloth from my aunt and put the tassels over my shoulders. She still requests a royal bow before serving dinner.

mbm-2523.clue: I only chalk half the number.
mbm-2523.quote: My training partner and I take turns writing each other's lifts on the slate. I draw the first stroke, she finishes the number. Even the numbers on our best days are shared.

mbm-2524.clue: The pockets paid for the whole coat.
mbm-2524.quote: I found a secondhand winter coat with separate little pockets for a pencil, a comb and what might have been a harmonica. I spent the rest of the market looking for the harmonica.

mbm-2525.clue: I pick up the tee before the ball lands.
mbm-2525.quote: My granddad rests a bright red tee on his golf cap so he can always find it. I copied him. Now when we walk down a fairway the people behind us see two little red flags.
